title: Hormisdas becomes bishop of Rome after Symmachus dies
description: Hormisdas was consecrated bishop of Rome the day after the death of Pope Symmachus, whose own tenure had been marked by a schism over his election. His papacy was dominated by the Acacian schism, which ended in 519 with the reunion of Constantinople and Rome.

title: Japanese divisions enter the abandoned city of Pyongyang
description: Japan's First and Third Divisions entered Pyongyang after its Korean defenders abandoned it overnight, capturing 100,000 tons of military supplies and grain. Ming reinforcements and the Joseon Navy later forced the Japanese out of the northern provinces.

title: An earthquake near Crete sends a tsunami across the Mediterranean
description: An undersea earthquake, estimated at magnitude 8.5 or higher with an assumed epicentre near Crete, destroyed nearly all of the island's towns. Its tsunami devastated Libya, Alexandria and the Nile Delta, killing thousands and hurling ships 3 km inland.

title: Pontian succeeds Urban I as bishop of Rome
description: Pontian became bishop of Rome in succession to Urban I, who had died in May. In 235, during the persecution of Christians under Emperor Maximinus Thrax, he was arrested and sent to Sardinia, and he became the first pope to resign his office.

title: Dionysius is elected bishop of Rome after Valerian's persecution
description: Dionysius was elected bishop of Rome almost a year after Pope Sixtus II was killed in Emperor Valerian's persecution of Christians. His pontificate saw the toleration issued by Gallienus in 260, and he assigned presbyters to individual parishes.

title: St. Mary Magdalene's flood strikes central Europe
description: The largest recorded flood in central Europe struck on and around the feast day of St. Mary Magdalene, and became known by her name. Its water levels exceeded those of the 2002 European floods, making it the worst such event on record for the region.

title: John V becomes pope without prior imperial consent
description: John V became bishop of Rome, the first pope of the Byzantine Papacy consecrated without prior imperial consent and the first of ten consecutive popes of Eastern origin. His short papacy was marked by reconciliation between Rome and the Empire.

title: Argentina and Chile sign their Boundary Treaty in Buenos Aires
description: Bernardo de Irigoyen for Argentina and Francisco de Borja Echeverría for Chile signed a treaty in Buenos Aires to fix a precise border. Though it divided largely unexplored lands, it laid the groundwork for nearly all of today's 5600 km border.
source: Boundary Treaty of 1881 between Chile and Argentina

title: Jubal Early drives Crook's Union army from the Shenandoah Valley
description: At the Second Battle of Kernstown, the Confederate Army of the Valley under Jubal Early defeated George Crook's Union army and drove it from the Shenandoah Valley over the Potomac. Early then launched the Confederacy's last major raid into Union territory.

title: Marshal Villars defeats Prince Eugene at Denain
description: In the War of the Spanish Succession, French forces under Marshal Villars won a victory at Denain over the Dutch and Austrian forces of Prince Eugene of Savoy. The war had begun over the throne of Charles II of Spain, who died in 1700 without children.

title: Troops at Eboracum proclaim Constantine augustus
description: After his father Constantius died at Eboracum (modern York), the Alamannic king Chrocus proclaimed Constantine augustus and the troops acclaimed him. Galerius granted him only the title caesar, which Constantine accepted to remove doubts about his legitimacy.

title: The Arch of Constantine is officially opened in Rome
description: The arch the Roman Senate dedicated to Constantine opened, marking ten years of his reign and his victory over Maxentius at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge in 312. Standing between the Colosseum and the Palatine Hill, it is the largest Roman triumphal arch.

title: The Continental Congress creates a postal system under Franklin
description: The Second Continental Congress created the United States Post Office by decree, after printers and the new political leadership had overthrown the London-oriented imperial postal service. Benjamin Franklin briefly headed it as postmaster general.

title: About sixty nobles die as a floor collapses at Erfurt
description: During a Hoftag held by King Henry VI at Erfurt, the floor of a building gave way under the combined weight of the assembled nobles and fell into the latrine cesspit below. About sixty local nobles died, some of them drowned in the human waste.

title: The Continental Congress establishes the Army Hospital
description: The Continental Congress established an "Army Hospital", overseen by a Director General and Chief Physician, to care for the Continental Army. The U.S. Army Medical Department traces its origins to it; a permanent Medical Department came in 1818.

title: Rudolph II and Adalbert of Ivrea defeat Berengar I at Fiorenzuola
description: The forces of Rudolph II of Burgundy and Adalbert I of Ivrea defeated Berengar I of Italy at Fiorenzuola, leaving Berengar de facto dethroned and Rudolph King of Italy. Berengar's own grandson, the later king Berengar II, fought on the winning side.

title: Vitalian becomes bishop of Rome after Eugene I
description: Vitalian became bishop of Rome after the death of Eugene I, amid the dispute between the papacy and Constantinople over Monothelitism, which Rome condemned. He kept a conciliatory relationship with Emperor Constans II, who visited him in Rome.

title: Columbus reaches Guanaja off Honduras on his fourth voyage
description: On his fourth voyage Christopher Columbus reached Guanaja in the Bay Islands off Honduras, where his brother Bartolomeo met native merchants, possibly Mayans, with a large canoe filled with cargo. The natives introduced Columbus and his men to cacao.

title: Sixtus III becomes bishop of Rome after Celestine I
description: Sixtus III became bishop of Rome four days after the death of Celestine I, who had been instrumental in the condemnation of Nestorius at the Council of Ephesus. Sixtus's papacy is associated with a period of increased construction in Rome.

title: Sergius IV becomes pope after John XVIII abdicates
description: Sergius IV became bishop of Rome and nominal ruler of the Papal States after the abdication of John XVIII, though his temporal power was eclipsed by the patrician John II Crescentius. Since his time, taking a new name on election has been a papal tradition.

title: Bishop Marinus opens the first Council of Arles
description: The first council of Arles, the first called by Constantine, was opened by presiding bishop Marinus a year after the Edict of Milan. It condemned Donatism as a heresy and ruled that Easter should be held on the same day throughout the world.

title: The first United States census counts the nation's population
description: The first United States census recorded the population of the whole country as of Census Day, as Article 1, Section 2, of the Constitution required. Taken under Secretary of State Thomas Jefferson, it counted 3,929,214 inhabitants.

title: Arab Shah's horde defeats the Russian princes on the Pyana River
description: On the Pyana River, the Golden Horde under Arab Shah (Arapsha) defeated an alliance of Russian principalities led by Prince Ivan Dmitriyevich. The alliance joined the Pereyaslavl, Yaroslavl, Yuryev, Nizhny Novgorod and Murom principalities.

title: The Treaty of Greenville ends the Northwest Indian War
description: At Fort Greenville, Ohio, Anthony Wayne for the United States and a coalition of Native American nations signed a treaty a year after the Native American loss at Fallen Timbers. It ended the Northwest Indian War and limited Indian country to northwestern Ohio.

title: Bishop Grimketel leads the beatification of Olaf of Norway
description: The English bishop Grimketel, whom Olaf had brought from England, led the translation and beatification of King Olaf a year after his death at Stiklestad. Pope Alexander III confirmed this local canonisation in 1164, making Olaf a recognised saint.

title: Congress creates the Revenue-Marine, forerunner of the Coast Guard
description: An Act of Congress established the Revenue-Marine, later the United States Revenue Cutter Service, on the recommendation of Alexander Hamilton, the nation's first secretary of the treasury. The service was the forerunner of the United States Coast Guard.

title: Caliph al-Muti' abdicates and his son al-Ta'i succeeds him
description: After the Turkic commander Sabuktakin seized Baghdad from the Buyid Izz al-Dawla, the aged and paralysed caliph al-Muti' was induced to abdicate. His son became caliph as al-Ta'i, the first father-to-son succession of the caliphate since 902.

title: Mercia and Wessex defeat a Viking army at Tettenhall
description: The allied forces of Mercia and Wessex under Edward the Elder and Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians, defeated Northumbrian Vikings near Tettenhall, according to the chronicler Æthelweard. It was the last major Danish army to raid England for nearly a century.

title: Pope Sixtus II is killed in Valerian's persecution
description: Pope Sixtus II, in office since 31 August 257, was arrested while celebrating mass and beheaded during the persecution of Christians by Emperor Valerian. Seven deacons were killed with him, among them Lawrence of Rome.

title: Antipope Constantine II is overthrown with Lombard help
description: Constantine II, a Roman prelate who had claimed the papacy since June 767, was overthrown through the intervention of the Lombards, whose troops blinded him. He was condemned and expelled from the Church at the Lateran Council of 769.

title: Stephen III is elected pope amid a contest of rival factions
description: Stephen III, a Benedictine monk, was elected bishop of Rome with the support of the Roman officials amid a tumultuous contest of rival factions. He summoned the Lateran Council of 769, which sought to limit the nobles' influence in papal elections.

title: The Shawnee of Wapakoneta give up their lands in Ohio
description: In the Treaty of Wapakoneta, four hundred Shawnee, remnants of the tribe at Wapakoneta, were forced to relinquish their claims to land in western Ohio. In exchange they were to receive land west of the Mississippi River.

title: The Creek sign the Treaty of Fort Jackson
description: The Creek signed the Treaty of Fort Jackson near Wetumpka, Alabama, after United States allied forces had defeated the Red Stick resistance at the Battle of Horseshoe Bend. Under the treaty they gave up huge parts of Alabama and Georgia.

title: A British–French fleet begins bombarding the fortress of Sveaborg
description: British and French ships began bombarding the Russian fortress of Sveaborg from beyond the range of its artillery, in the Åland War, the Baltic Sea theater of the Crimean War. After 48 hours of bombardment the attackers withdrew without attempting a landing.

title: Jaume Ferrer sails from Majorca for the River of Gold
description: The Majorcan sailor Jaume Ferrer set out from Majorca to find the "River of Gold", the Senegal River. The outcome of his quest and his fate are unknown; he is memorialized in his native city of Palma.

title: Eugene I becomes pope after Constans II banishes Martin I
description: Eugene I was chosen bishop of Rome after Emperor Constans II had Martin I arrested, carried off to Constantinople and banished to Cherson for his strong opposition to Monothelitism. Eugene held the office until his death on 2 June 657.

title: The general Silvanus declares himself emperor at Cologne
description: Fearing punishment from Constantius II after forged letters had made him appear a traitor, the general Silvanus declared himself emperor at Colonia Agrippina (modern Cologne). Bribed soldiers later murdered him on his way to a Christian church service.

title: Edward Balliol's English-backed force routs the Scots at Dupplin Moor
description: Near Perth, a Scottish force under Donald, Earl of Mar, possibly as many as 40,000 men, attacked about 1,500 largely English troops under Edward Balliol and was routed. It was the first major battle of the Second War of Scottish Independence.

title: Nur ad-Din crushes a Crusader and Byzantine army at Harim
description: At Harim in Syria, Nur ad-Din won a crushing victory over a combined army from the County of Tripoli, the Principality of Antioch, the Byzantine Empire and Armenia. Most of the leaders of the opposing army were captured.

title: Charles of Lorraine defeats the Ottoman army at Mohács
description: The forces of Leopold I, Holy Roman Emperor, under Charles of Lorraine met the army of Sultan Mehmed IV under the Grand Vizier Sarı Süleyman Pasha at Mohács, in the battle also called Harsány Mountain. The result was a decisive victory for the Austrians.

title: Brazilian troops massacre a Paraguayan force of boys at Acosta Ñu
description: At Acosta Ñu, 3,500 poorly armed Paraguayans, mostly boys of nine to fifteen, old men and wounded combatants, faced 20,000 Brazilian and Argentine veterans and were massacred. It was the last major engagement of the Paraguayan War.

title: A great earthquake devastates northern Anatolia
description: An earthquake with an estimated magnitude of 7.8 to 8.0, centred on the southern shore of Ladik Lake, struck northern Anatolia. It caused widespread damage from Bolu to Erzincan and about 8,000 deaths, and is thought to be the strongest in Turkey.

title: Cesare Borgia resigns as cardinal and becomes Duke of Valentinois
description: Cesare Borgia, son of Pope Alexander VI, resigned from the cardinalate to pursue a military career, the first person to do so. The same day King Louis XII of France named him Duke of Valentinois, a title chosen as homophonous with his nickname Il Valentino.

title: Lezgin tribesmen sack Shamakhi, the capital of Shirvan
description: Sunni Lezgins led by Haji Davud Bey took Shamakhi, the capital of the Safavid province of Shirvan, after the central government abandoned its counter-campaign at a critical moment. The 15,000 tribesmen massacred the city's Shia population and ransacked it.

title: Union troops strike the Weldon Railroad at Globe Tavern
description: South of Petersburg, Virginia, a Union force under Gouverneur K. Warren destroyed miles of the Weldon Railroad and withstood strong Confederate attacks. It was the first Union victory of the Richmond–Petersburg Campaign.

title: Fabius Gurges dedicates Rome's first temple of Venus
description: During the Third Samnite War, Quintus Fabius Maximus Gurges dedicated the first Roman temple of Venus, to Venus Obsequens, near the Aventine Hill and the Circus Maximus. It was supposedly funded by fines imposed on women found guilty of adultery.

skip: lead only, one sentence (Pius II pope from 19 August 1458 to 1464): the material cannot carry two sentences

title: Henry IV of Castile and his half-brother Alfonso clash at Olmedo
description: Near Olmedo in Castile, the forces of Henry IV of Castile met those of his half-brother Alfonso, Prince of Asturias, in their succession war. Alfonso, whom Henry had recognized as heir presumptive, was the figurehead of the rebelling Castilian magnates.

title: Wang Yangming captures the Prince of Ning, ending his rebellion
description: The government army led by Wang Yangming, grand coordinator of southern Jiangxi, captured Zhu Chenhao, Prince of Ning, ending his rebellion against the Zhengde Emperor. The prince was sentenced to execution, but the emperor commuted the sentence to suicide.

title: Eraclus is consecrated bishop of Liège
description: Eraclus, dean of Bonn, was consecrated the 25th bishop of Liège after his election with the support of Bruno of Cologne. He founded the collegiate churches of St Paul's and St Martin's and laid the foundations for Liège as an international centre of learning.

title: A janissary revolt deposes Sultan Mustafa II
description: In the Edirne Incident, a janissary revolt against the consequences of the Treaty of Karlowitz and the sultan's absence from the capital, Mustafa II was deposed and his brother Ahmed III became sultan. The rebels killed the Şeyhülislam Feyzullah Efendi.

title: José de La Mar becomes constitutional president of Peru
description: José de La Mar, a military leader born in Cuenca in present-day Ecuador, became Constitutional President of Peru. His two years in office brought several uprisings and conspiracies and armed conflicts with the new Republic of Bolivia and with Gran Colombia.

title: Selim I defeats Shah Ismail I at Chaldiran
description: The Ottoman Empire under Selim I won a decisive victory over the Safavid Empire of Ismail I at Chaldiran and annexed Eastern Anatolia and Upper Mesopotamia. It began 41 years of war between the two empires, ended in 1555 by the Peace of Amasya.

title: A priest at Philae carves the last known hieroglyphic inscription
description: In the temple of Philae in southern Egypt, the priest Nesmeterakhem carved a figure of the god Mandulis and a text hoping it would last "for all time and eternity". It is the last known ancient Egyptian inscription in Egyptian hieroglyphs.

title: Selim I defeats the Mamluk Sultanate at Marj Dabiq
description: Near Dabiq, 44 km north of Aleppo, the Ottoman army of Selim I defeated the Mamluk Sultanate. The victory gave Selim's armies control of the entire region of Syria and opened the door to the conquest of Egypt and the end of the Mamluk Sultanate.

title: Marcian is proclaimed Eastern Roman emperor at Hebdomon
description: Marcian, a domesticus who had served the commanders Ardabur and Aspar for fifteen years, was elected and inaugurated emperor of the East after the death of Theodosius II. Theodosius's sister Pulcheria had agreed, after a month of negotiations, to marry him.

title: The New York Sun begins the Great Moon Hoax
description: The New York newspaper The Sun published the first of six articles about the supposed discovery of life and civilization on the Moon. The discoveries were falsely attributed to Sir John Herschel and his fictitious companion Andrew Grant.

title: Alauddin Khalji takes Chittor Fort after an eight-month siege
description: Alauddin Khalji of the Delhi Sultanate entered Chittor Fort, taken from the Guhila king Ratnasimha, and ordered a general massacre of its people; Amir Khusrau put the dead at 30,000, a figure one historian calls probably an exaggeration.

title: Lutherans in Philadelphia found the Pennsylvania Ministerium
description: Encouraged by Henry Melchior Muhlenberg, Lutheran clergy meeting in Philadelphia founded the Pennsylvania Ministerium, the first Lutheran church body in North America. Until 1792 it was called the German Evangelical Lutheran Ministerium of North America.

title: Henry the Young King is crowned again, with Margaret of France
description: At Winchester Cathedral Henry, eldest surviving son of Henry II, was crowned King of England a second time, now with his wife Margaret of France. Leaving her out of his first coronation in 1170 had almost certainly been a calculated insult to Louis VII.

title: The Aragonese and Venetian fleet crushes Genoa off Alghero
description: Off Alghero in northwestern Sardinia, the allied fleet of the Crown of Aragon and the Republic of Venice crushed the fleet of the Republic of Genoa, capturing most of it. Genoa was at war with Venice and backed Sardinian rebels against Aragonese rule.

title: Theodoric defeats Odoacer on the Isonzo and enters Italy
description: Sent by Emperor Zeno to overthrow Odoacer, king of Italy, Theodoric won a battle on the banks of the Isontius River (now the Isonzo), not far from Aquileia, soon after arriving in Italy. A victory at Verona followed the same year, and by 493 he ruled Italy.

title: Pamheiba is crowned king of Manipur
description: Pamheiba was crowned Meidingu (king) of Manipur, which he ruled as Gharib Niwaz until 1748. He introduced Hinduism as the state religion in 1717, renamed the kingdom from Kangleipak to Manipur in 1724 and fought the Burmese for most of his reign.

title: Guru Arjan completes the compilation of the Adi Granth
description: Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh guru, completed the compilation of the Adi Granth, the first rendition of the Sikh scripture later known as the Guru Granth Sahib. It was first installed in the Golden Temple in Amritsar on 1 September 1604.

title: Jetha becomes the fourth Sikh guru as Guru Ram Das
description: Jetha became the fourth Sikh guru, known as Guru Ram Das, and held the office for seven years. He was the first of Guru Nanak's successors to rekindle ties with Nanak's son Sri Chand, after a long estrangement between mainstream Sikhs and the Udasis.

title: Red Stick Creek warriors storm Fort Mims in Alabama
description: In the Creek War, a large force of the Red Sticks faction under Peter McQueen and William Weatherford stormed Fort Mims, north of Mobile, Alabama, and defeated its militia garrison. Over 500 settlers were killed, among them over 250 armed militia.

title: A great earthquake in the Atacama sends tsunamis to Hawaii and Japan
description: An earthquake estimated at magnitude 8.8 to 9.4 shook the southern Atacama Desert, causing tsunamis in Chile as well as Hawaii and Japan. In the Japanese harbours of Kawarago and Aiga, residents saw the water recede without any sign of an earthquake.

skip: the material dates the Synod of Constantinople from 1 September 1483 to 31 August 1484, not to 31 August 1483

title: Camillus dedicates the temple of Juno Regina on the Aventine
description: Marcus Furius Camillus dedicated a temple on the Aventine Hill to "Juno, Queen of Veii", vowed on his conquest of Veii, and placed in it a statue of the goddess brought from that city. It was later noted for its gifts, sacrifices and miracles.

title: Congress creates the United States Department of the Treasury
description: The First United States Congress created a Department of Treasury, headed by a Secretary of the Treasury, to manage government finances. Alexander Hamilton became the first secretary and insisted on repaying the country's $75 million debt.
source: United States Department of the Treasury

title: The Tianjing Incident tears apart the Taiping leadership
description: In Tianjing, capital of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, a conflict among its leaders killed the East King Yang Xiuqing, the North King Wei Changhui and more than 27,000 others. It is said to have been the turning point toward the rebellion's failure.

title: King Wamba takes Nîmes from the rebel Duke Paul
description: The Visigothic king Wamba secured the surrender of Nîmes, where Duke Paul, sent to end the revolt of Hilderic, count of Nîmes, had himself become the rebels' leader. Paul and the other rebel leaders were tried three days later, scalped and imprisoned for life.

title: American and German troops clash at Cooch's Bridge in Delaware
description: The Continental Army and American militia fought primarily German soldiers serving with the British Army at Cooch's Bridge, the only significant action of the war in Delaware. Some traditions claim it as the first battle that saw the U.S. flag.

skip: lead only: the Treaty of Kerden between the Ottoman Empire and Afsharid Iran ended the 1743-1746 war; nothing more to carry two sentences

title: Peter III of Aragon is proclaimed King of Sicily in Palermo
description: After the Sicilian Vespers rising against Charles I of Anjou, Sicilian rebels offered Peter the crown, holding his wife Constance their rightful queen, and he was proclaimed king in Palermo. Charles fled across the Straits of Messina to his Kingdom of Naples.

title: Gregory IX promulgates his Decretals with the bull Rex pacificus
description: Pope Gregory IX issued the bull Rex pacificus for a new collection of canon law, compiled by the Dominican Raymond of Peñafort to replace the Decretum Gratiani. The Decretals remained a major part of Church law until the 1917 Code of Canon Law.

title: Potawatomi and Miami warriors lay siege to Fort Wayne
description: In the War of 1812, warriors under the Potawatomi chiefs Winamac and Five Medals killed two men of the U.S. garrison at Fort Wayne, beginning a siege by Potawatomi and Miami forces. Winamac withdrew ahead of reinforcements under William Henry Harrison.

title: Louisa Ann Swain casts her ballot in Laramie, Wyoming
description: Louisa Ann Swain voted in a general election in Laramie, Wyoming. She was the first woman in the United States to do so since the repeal of women's suffrage in New Jersey in 1807.

title: Mormon militiamen attack an emigrant wagon train at Mountain Meadows
description: Utah militiamen disguised as Native Americans, with some Southern Paiutes, attacked the Baker–Fancher wagon train, mostly families from Arkansas. After a five-day siege they murdered at least 120 emigrants, sparing only seventeen young children.
links: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

skip: the article dates only Antipope Clement III's death to 8 September 1100, not the night election of Theodoric that followed

title: Constantine's three sons are named augusti and divide the empire
description: Constantine II, Constantius II and Constans were named augusti when they met in Pannonia and divided the Roman territories among themselves; Constantine II received Gaul, Britannia and Hispania. He was left unsatisfied, believing his age gave him seniority.

title: Byzantine forces defeat the Principality of Achaea at Saint George
description: At the fortress of Saint George in Skorta, the forces of the Byzantine governor of Mystras, Andronikos Asen, ambushed and defeated those of the Latin Principality of Achaea. As a result Arcadia, the heartland of the Morea, came firmly under Byzantine control.

title: Celestine I is elected bishop of Rome after Boniface I
description: Celestine I was elected bishop of Rome after the death of Boniface I, and spent his pontificate largely combatting teachings deemed heretical. He was instrumental in the condemnation of Nestorius at the Council of Ephesus.

title: Fifty-five Catholics are executed in Nagasaki
description: In the Great Genna Martyrdom, 55 foreign and domestic Catholics were executed together at Nishizaka Hill in Nagasaki, after a smuggling incident involving two foreign missionaries. It was part of the persecution of Christians by the shogun Tokugawa Hidetada.
